title: A fly whole-brain spiking model built from three connectomes gives FlyWire and male CNS taste responses that agree almost as well as within one map; looming and BANC responses agree much less
abstract: Question: when the Shiu et al. 2024 leaky integrate-and-fire model of the whole fly brain is built from three adult connectomes (FlyWire 783, BANC 888, male CNS v1.0), which responses stay the same, and how does between-fly agreement compare with agreement between two stimulus subsets in one map? Approach: a numba re-implementation of the published model (neuron-level rate r = 0.999 against the original Brian2 code; MN9 62.4 vs 63.0 Hz). We stimulated complete populations of six sensory types (sugar, water, sugar/low-salt, bitter, LC4, LPLC2) at 150 Hz, 30 trials, in 132 conditions. The primary model matches the mean input synapse count of each cell type to FlyWire and uses FlyWire-type transmitter signs. Results: in all three maps sugar drove the feeding motor neuron MN9 (63.9, 34.1, 93.1 Hz), bitter input stopped it, and LC4 drove the giant fibre and DNp02, DNp04 and DNp11 (rates differ up to 5.5 times). With equal-size disjoint stimulus subsets, FlyWire and male CNS type-level response profiles agreed at 0.79-0.83 of the within-map agreement for taste input, but at only 0.37-0.48 for looming input, although looming responses were the most reproducible inside each map (r = 0.89-0.95). Pairs with BANC agreed less for all inputs (median ratio 0.35). Raw synapse counts failed: BANC sugar gave 0 Hz at MN9 and the male CNS went into a Kenyon-cell runaway state in all trials. Removal of connections with fewer than 5 synapses, weight multipliers 0.7-1.4 and the nerve cord did not remove the BANC gap. Limitations: the maps differ in sex, individual and reconstruction method, so biological and technical variation are not separated; the within-map reference has only 1-2 subset pairs per map and input; stimulation was bilateral. Our code, aggregate results and figures are included; external connectome data are not bundled but have a hash-checked retrieval script.

Left: Jaccard overlap of active cell types; right: Pearson r of log rates. FlyWire-male CNS taste responses agree almost at the within-map level; looming responses and pairs with BANC agree much less.

Behavioural read-outs of the same LIF model built from FlyWire 783, BANC 888 and male CNS v1.0 (type-matched input, FlyWire-type signs). Sugar drives MN9 and bitter stops it in all maps; LC4 drives all four looming descending neurons; rates differ between maps. Labels give the number of ignited (runaway) trials of 30.

Effect of calibration steps on sugar-to-MN9 and LC4-to-giant-fibre drive. Raw synapse counts give no MN9 drive in BANC and runaway in the male CNS; BANC needs both type-matched input and FlyWire-type signs.

Supports lower FlyWire-BANC agreement and the failure of gain, sign and nerve-cord fixes; qualifies its conclusion that sparse responses do not transfer, because FlyWire and male CNS taste responses transfer at about 0.8 of the within-map level with population input.
Independent support that sugar-to-MN9 drive transfers to BANC and male CNS and that BANC agrees less.
